title: What does a supportive response mean to you?
starting_idea: I want to identify replies that make someone feel supported, even when people express support differently.

sources.text: I want to identify replies that make someone feel supported, even when people express support differently.
sources.provenance: Synthetic human brief for this prototype; not a recorded user quote.

sources.text: G0-demo: label a reply as supportive when it offers meaningful support. Boundaries, exceptions, and review actions are not yet defined.
sources.provenance: Authored demo baseline; not an approved guideline.

sources.text: L01–L10 are invented contrastive examples. They illustrate rule-level decisions rather than individual gold-label requests.
sources.provenance: Synthetic learning-only examples; no retrieval or model experiment has run.

decisions.title: Can practical help count without emotional reassurance?
decisions.why: The current phrase ‘meaningful support’ leaves practical advice open to interpretation.
decisions.current_rule: No distinction between emotional reassurance and practical assistance.
decisions.scope: Replies that offer relevant practical help without explicitly validating feelings.

examples.context: I feel overwhelmed by tomorrow’s interview.
examples.reply: Try one practice interview tonight. I can help you rehearse.

examples.context: I feel overwhelmed by tomorrow’s interview.
examples.reply: That sounds stressful. It makes sense to feel nervous.

options.label: Either kind of support can count
options.effect: Recognize relevant practical assistance or emotional reassurance; neither is individually required.

options.label: Emotional reassurance is required
options.effect: Practical help alone does not satisfy the supportive label.

options.label: Keep the two kinds as separate labels
options.effect: Propose separate emotional-support and practical-support labels; the label schema will need review.

decisions.title: What if useful advice also dismisses the person’s feelings?
decisions.why: A rule about helpful content may conflict with your preference about how people are treated.
decisions.current_rule: No precedence rule for useful advice paired with dismissive language.
decisions.scope: Replies combining practical help with dismissive or belittling wording.

examples.context: I am anxious about asking for more time.
examples.reply: Stop being dramatic. Just email them for an extension.

examples.context: I am anxious about asking for more time.
examples.reply: You could email them for an extension, if that would help.

options.label: Dismissal overrides helpful content
options.effect: Label the combination as not supportive; explain the dismissal exception in the guideline.

options.label: Use a mixed-support label
options.effect: Preserve both aspects through a proposed mixed label, subject to schema review.

options.label: Relevant help can still count
options.effect: Helpful content may satisfy support; record dismissive tone as a separate diagnostic.

decisions.title: Should an unclear reply receive a label or wait for context?
decisions.why: Uncertainty caused by missing evidence should not silently become a negative label.
decisions.current_rule: No specified action when the available item cannot support a reliable interpretation.
decisions.scope: Items whose interpretation depends on unavailable surrounding conversation.

examples.context: Can you stay with me while I call?
examples.reply: Sure. Whatever you need. I will stay right here.

options.label: Defer the task label and request context
options.effect: Use insufficient-evidence status; missing evidence is not a not-supportive label.

options.label: Apply a literal-reading convention
options.effect: Define a literal-reading policy explicitly and still record missing context.

options.label: Make a provisional label and flag review
options.effect: Keep the prediction separate from accepted labels until the uncertainty is resolved.

decisions.title: What should a ‘hard case’ tag actually mean?
decisions.why: A long reply can be easy to label; a short reply can contain a difficult boundary.
decisions.current_rule: Difficulty has no operational definition yet.
decisions.scope: Diagnostic tags accompanying the task label; these tags are not correctness claims.

examples.reply: That sounds exhausting. I can listen, help with dinner, or give you space. You can choose what helps most.
At least you have a job.

options.label: Difficulty means competing plausible interpretations
options.effect: Mark hard when more than one interpretation remains plausible under the current rules.

options.label: Difficulty means substantial review effort
options.effect: Track reviewer effort separately from uncertainty and correctness.

options.label: Record ambiguity and effort separately
options.effect: Use two diagnostic fields, with separate criteria and an unknown state.

decisions.title: Can a reply disagree and still be supportive?
decisions.why: Agreement with a viewpoint and support for a person may be different dimensions.
decisions.current_rule: No rule distinguishes disagreement from dismissal.
decisions.scope: Replies that challenge a position while responding to the person’s needs.

examples.context: I think I should cut off my friend over one missed call.
examples.reply: I understand why you are hurt. I would talk with them first, and I can help you think through what to say.

examples.context: I think I should cut off my friend over one missed call.
examples.reply: That is ridiculous. You are always overreacting.

options.label: Support does not require agreement
options.effect: Evaluate acknowledgment and help independently of agreement with the person’s position.

options.label: Disagreement requires explicit acknowledgment
options.effect: When a reply disagrees, require acknowledgment of the person’s feelings or perspective.

options.label: Track agreement separately
options.effect: Add an agreement dimension without using it as a substitute for support.

decisions.title: After you confirm a rule, how should affected labels be handled?
decisions.why: Approving a rule does not mean you individually reviewed every label produced with it.
decisions.current_rule: No explicit acceptance policy for labels inferred from newly approved rules.
decisions.scope: Affected learning items and later large-scale predictions; item provenance must remain visible.

options.label: Review affected items individually
options.effect: Re-label affected items, then request individual review before accepting them.

options.label: Use a separately specified batch-audit policy
options.effect: Draft audit sampling, tolerances and acceptance gates for approval; labels remain provisional until those gates are defined and passed.

options.label: Keep them provisional for now
options.effect: Use new predictions for further exploration without promoting them to approved reference labels.
